title: Vowels and letter pairs
goal: Read the two-letter spellings and apply the αυ/ευ rule.

blocks.text:
Greek has only **five vowel sounds**, [i e a o u], but many ways to write them. The sound [i] alone has six spellings: ι, η, υ, ει, οι, υι. This is why Greeks talk about writing 'with an ήτα' or 'with a γιώτα': the spelling carries grammar and history, not sound.

Several consonant sounds that English writes with one letter need two in Greek: [b] is μπ, [d] is ντ, [g] is γκ.

blocks.title: One sound, several spellings
head: Sound
Spellings
rows: ι, η, υ, ει, οι, υι

blocks.text: **The αυ / ευ rule.** Before a vowel or a voiced consonant (β δ γ ζ λ ρ μ ν), υ is [v]: αύριο [ávrio], ευρώ [evró]. Before a voiceless consonant (π τ κ φ θ χ σ ξ ψ) or at the end of a word, it is [f]: αυτός [aftós], ευχαριστώ [efxaristó].

blocks.title: Why Greeks spell by history
blocks.text: Because sound no longer decides spelling, Greek schoolchildren practise **ορθογραφία** 'spelling', usually as dictation, for years, and adults still argue over i-sounds. Homophones are everywhere: **κλείνω** 'I close' and **κλίνω** 'I decline (a noun)', **τοίχος** 'wall' and **τείχος** 'city wall', **πήρα** 'I took' and **πείρα** 'experience'. The 1982 reform (μονοτονικό) dropped breathings and extra accents but kept these historical spellings. Borrowed words show the letter pairs at work: foreign b, d, g arrive as μπ, ντ, γκ, in **μπαρ** 'bar', **ντους** 'shower' and **γκολ** 'goal'.

blocks.title: Sounds across word boundaries
blocks.cite: Holton §1.6. Final ν of τον, την, δεν, μην merges with the next word in speech.

items.why: υ in αυ/ευ is [v] before a vowel or a voiced consonant such as ρ.
Before a voiceless consonant (here τ) αυ is [af].
αι is a single [e] sound.
ου is a single [u] sound.
μπ is [b]; inside a word careful speakers may say [mb], never [mp].
Word-initial ντ is [d].
Word-initial γκ is [ɡ]; a single γ would be [ɣ].
γγ is always [ŋɡ], as in *anger*.
An accent on the first letter of αι (or a diaeresis on ι) splits it into two vowels; τσ is [ts].
ει is just [i]; the accent on ί marks the stress, not a separate vowel.
[b] is spelled μπ, both at the start and inside the word.
[d] is spelled ντ; δ would be [ð].
[ɡ] is spelled γκ; one-syllable words take no accent.

items.prompt: Write in Greek: [ávrio] 'tomorrow' (spelled with αυ, ending -ιο)
items.why: The accent of a stressed αυ goes on the second letter: αύ.
[ef] before voiceless χ is ευ.
αι = [e]; the final stressed [i] here is ί.
[u] is always ου; there is no single letter for it.

items.prompt: Write in Greek: [ðulévo] 'I work' (ου, ευ, ending -ω)
items.why: [ev] before a vowel is ευ; the accent goes on its second letter: εύ.
The accent on α shows that α and ι are pronounced separately.
[b] = μπ. The older spelling μπύρα is still common.
